vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: new-agent
Version: 1.1.0

The skill bundle is a legitimate utility for automating the setup of OpenClaw agents and their messaging channel configurations (Telegram, Discord, etc.). The primary script, `scripts/setup-agent.sh`, performs standard local file operations like creating directories and template markdown files within the user's `~/.openclaw` directory, and the instructions in `SKILL.md` are consistent with the stated purpose of agent management.

llm.summary: The skill's code and instructions match its stated purpose (creating a workspace, registering an agent, and configuring a messaging channel); nothing requests unrelated credentials or installs arbitrary code.

dimensions.detail: Name and description (create/register an OpenClaw agent and connect a channel) align with the included files: SKILL.md explains workspace/registration/channel steps and scripts/setup-agent.sh implements workspace creation and registration. The CLI calls and config edits are expected for this functionality.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions tell the user/agent to edit openclaw.json and to supply channel credentials (bot tokens, app secrets, QR scans) — this is necessary for connecting channels. The SKILL.md and the script write files into ~/.openclaw workspace and ask the user to update openclaw.json with account/binding entries; that is in-scope but the agent will be working with gateway configuration files which contain potentially sensitive data, so users should review changes before applying them.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or remote downloads. This is an instruction-only skill with a local helper script; nothing in the package pulls code from external URLs or creates binaries.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, and the script respects OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR if present (defaults to ~/.openclaw). The script copies and reads openclaw.json (gateway config) — which may contain shared model credentials or other sensitive entries — but reading/updating that file is expected for agent registration. Users should confirm where channel credentials will be stored and who can access openclaw.json backups.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request persistent platform privileges beyond creating a workspace and adding an agent entry in the gateway config. It doesn't modify other skills' configs or enable itself globally.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill looks coherent for creating and registering an OpenClaw agent, but before running the script: (1) inspect scripts/setup-agent.sh yourself to confirm behavior (it copies openclaw.json and writes files under ~/.openclaw by default); (2) back up your gateway config and verify where you'll store channel tokens/app secrets (openclaw.json may contain other credentials); (3) be prepared to supply channel tokens or perform interactive QR logins as required; and (4) if you prefer, make the changes manually rather than running the helper script to retain full control.
